A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–4, and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching despite pagination and formatting differences.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 logistic-regression experiments in Figures 2–3 and inversion-bias experiments in Appendix G.3, Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 reports updated logistic-regression results in Figures 2–3 and retains the original inversion-bias experiments in Appendix G.3, Figure 4.

M1.justification: The debiasing matrix in (5), scalar leverage/SRHT corrections, and SSN update in (10) remain unchanged. The added heuristic explanations do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST and CIFAR-10 for binary logistic regression and inversion-bias evaluation. Appendix G.2 retains the same data dimensions and grouping of classes; no additional dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the same comparisons involving Newton-LESS, GD, SGD, ARLev, ALev, SLev, and SRHT. Figure 4 retains RLev, ARLev, and DARLev with and without scalar debiasing. Newly cited shrinkage methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G.1 change the timing protocol for Figures 2–3: v1 excludes input preprocessing, whereas v2 includes it and explicitly includes sketching overhead. This substantially changes the efficiency evaluation, while the stated data dimensions, regularization, sketch sizes, and iteration budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 2 revises the timing evidence in the existing sketch-size sensitivity analysis through fuller cost accounting. The exact-versus-approximate leverage and debiasing analysis in Appendix G.3 remains unchanged; no additional robustness or ablation study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 30 independent runs for Figure 2, 10 for Figure 3 except deterministic GD, and 500 for Figure 4. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 substantially replace the timing results. Figure 2's MNIST Newton-LESS timing curve becomes nearly flat rather than strongly increasing, and Figure 3 shows a much wider LESS–SRHT timing gap. Figure 2's relative-error values also change. The timings use revised accounting and do not establish same-protocol speed gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 expands the derivation of (27) with intermediate matrix-norm inequalities and explicit conditions supporting the factor 38. The formal results and rates remain unchanged. The main-text heuristic derivations reproduce reasoning already present in Appendices D.1 and E.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: characterizing and correcting sampling inversion bias, covering leverage sampling and SRHT, and establishing problem-independent local SSN convergence rates.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds dependent sampling, particularly volume sampling, as a possible extension with efficiency and convergence benefits. Existing empirical interpretations are largely retained, including descriptions of LESS runtime growth and close SRHT–LESS timings that fit the updated plots less well.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds an explicit pointer to Dereziński et al.'s public repository for implementation details, including SRHT. Existing descriptions of preprocessing, sampling construction, regularization, and Armijo line search are retained.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Zhang and Pilanci (2023) and Romanov et al. (2024), distinguishing shrinkage correction from modifying the sketch. Section 6 adds Cortinovis and Kressner (2024) when discussing dependent sampling. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 brings existing appendix heuristics into Section 3, clarifies the distinction between embedding error and inversion bias, edits introductory wording, shortens the displayed title to use SSN, and adds an Impact Statement. The overall section organization remains stable.

P2.justification: The four-figure structure is retained. Figures 2–3 have revised axis scales and sizing, with associated changes to figure placement and page breaks. Figures 1 and 4 preserve their substantive displays; there is no broad layout redesign.

improvement.justification: Including preprocessing and sketching costs makes the practical efficiency evaluation more informative. Main-text heuristics, expanded proof steps, and the implementation pointer also improve accessibility. These are limited gains around an unchanged theoretical contribution; retained prose about runtime growth and the SRHT–LESS gap is not fully reconciled with the revised plots.
